journey.name: Starter: send NIGHT
journey.description:
The whole send wizard, end to end, on the only path a user has to move NIGHT: pick the token and its privacy pool, address it, size it, review it, confirm it. Four screens, each of which can break on its own, and the last of which spends.
The app reporting "Sent" is the app's claim. The chain's is the recipient's balance, so this journey is only half the test: `scripts/money-journeys.sh prepare` records what the recipient holds beforehand and prints the address to send to, and `money-journeys.sh verify 1` afterwards fails unless the chain moved the NIGHT. Run both around this journey — a transaction that is submitted and never lands reads exactly like a success on screen.
Two things the screen tells the truth about by omission: - fees come out of Dust, not NIGHT, so there is no fee line to show and none is invented; - no transaction hash is shown, because the SDK currently reports an empty one. The transaction does finalize; there is just nothing on screen to look it up by, and the journey asserts what is actually there rather than pinning that gap shut.
Localnet, not a public testnet: see 05-receive-night.xml. The NIGHT ping-pongs between two wallets the operator controls and never leaves.
One harness trap, which is why this journey checks the address field before advancing: a single `adb shell input text` of a 77-character bech32m address DROPS characters on an emulator, in the middle of the string rather than at the end — 14 of 77 in one attempt, 5 in another. The wizard's client-side check only looks at the prefix, so a mangled address passes it and fails later inside the SDK, where it reads as a broken send rather than a broken keystroke. Type it a character at a time, and verify the field before tapping Next.
Preconditions this journey does NOT set up, and fails honestly without: - a debuggable build whose local.properties sets kuira.dev.seed; - a ledger-8 localnet answering on the pinned endpoints (`mn localnet up`); - `scripts/money-journeys.sh prepare`, which funds the wallet and prints the recipient; - the app set to the localnet network.
Dust is the one precondition the journey DOES set up, because a funded wallet does not have any yet and the send cannot pay its fee without it: registration is one tap in the wallet sheet, and the dust it generates takes a minute or two to show up.
Verified end to end on localnet 2026-10-24, twice: dust registered and generated 153.15, both proofs proved locally on the emulator, the transaction finalized in block 124ad025…, the pill fell from 10,499 to 10,498 NIGHT, and `money-journeys.sh verify 1` confirmed the recipient's balance moved on chain.

actions.action: If a notification permission prompt is shown, decline it
If a "Keep your wallet synced" backup offer is shown, choose "Not now"
If the screen shows a "Register" control, tap it and wait for the DUST figure to rise above zero
Verify the DUST figure shown is above zero
Note the NIGHT balance currently shown
Verify the screen shows a "Send" control
Verify the screen shows "Unshielded · Visible on chain"
Verify the screen shows "Shielded · Private · ZK proof"
Tap the "Unshielded · Visible on chain" row
Enter the recipient address printed by money-journeys.sh prepare into the address field
Verify the address field holds that recipient address in full, character for character
Verify the screen shows "Network fees are paid automatically from your Dust."
Verify the screen does NOT show "Send failed"
Verify the screen shows a "Done" control
Verify the NIGHT balance shown is one lower than the noted value
